knowledge_point.title: Computing a Reciprocal Ratio Using the Pythagorean Identity

question.:question/problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186110756/plots/04873f8ac682f45aff5b6458a4bad51ad7a89b024f29c457bbba23923a79ccbe.png)

The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that the $y$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $\frac{1}{5}$, use the Pythagorean identity to find $\sec\theta$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186110756/plots/aa2015710ab05e54479fc239230d578eaf84d14f99dc94496b9a5aab47d52b5d.png)

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta$ as follows:

$$x=\cos\theta,\qquad y=\sin\theta.$$

We're given that $y=\frac{1}{5}$ at the point $P$. Therefore, we have

$$\sin\theta=\frac{1}{5}.$$

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $\cos\theta$:

$$\begin{aligned}
\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta &= 1 \\
\cos^2\theta &= 1-\sin^2\theta \\
\cos\theta &= \pm\sqrt{1-\sin^2\theta}.
\end{aligned}$$

Substituting $\sin\theta=\frac{1}{5}$ gives

$$\begin{aligned}
\cos\theta &= \pm\sqrt{1-\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^2} \\
&=\pm\sqrt{1-\frac{1}{25}} \\
&=\pm\sqrt{\frac{24}{25}} \\
&=\pm \frac{2 \sqrt{6}}{5}.
\end{aligned}$$

We select the positive answer since $\cos\theta$ is positive in the first quadrant. So, $\cos\theta=\frac{2 \sqrt{6}}{5}$.

Knowing that $\sec\theta=\dfrac{1}{\cos\theta}$, we have

$$\sec\theta=\frac{1}{\frac{2 \sqrt{6}}{5}}=\frac{5}{2 \sqrt{6}}.$$

Finally, we rationalize the denominator.

$$\begin{aligned}
\sec\theta &= \frac{5}{2 \sqrt{6}} \\
&=\frac{5}{2 \sqrt{6}}\cdot\frac{2 \sqrt{6}}{2 \sqrt{6}} \\
&=\frac{5\,2 \sqrt{6}}{24} \\
&=\frac{5 \sqrt{6}}{12}.
\end{aligned}$$
